title: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 ISMS (add-on)
description: An information security management system on top of the Core registers and the ISO/IEC 27001:2022 requirement library: the ISMS scope and context and the risk treatment plan as its own sheets, and the information security risk category, Annex A links, residual risk, the ISMS documents, security incidents with a 24-hour containment clock, ISMS nonconformities, audits, reviews and training on the shared registers. Installs the Core registers (Full) first. The statement of applicability comes from the library. Reference numbers and short titles only, never the text of the standard.

sheets.name: ISMS scope and context
sheets.description: What shapes your ISMS: internal and external issues, the interested parties and what they need from you, the interfaces with what others run for you, and the scope statement. Link each entry to the clause it answers. Top management approves the scope statement with the Scope approval workflow.

fields.name: Clause
fields.description: The clause this entry answers: 4.1 for issues, 4.2 for interested parties, 4.3 for the scope.

fields.name: What they need from us
fields.description: For an interested party: what they expect, and which of those needs the ISMS takes on.

fields.name: How the ISMS answers it
fields.description: The risks, controls, objectives or documents that deal with this entry.

fields.name: Approval step
fields.description: Where the entry is in its approval. Set by the Scope approval workflow, never by hand.

items.name: Example: we depend on one cloud provider for every customer system

values.details: An outage or a change in their terms would stop our service.
values.response: Risk "Example: key supplier outage stops the service"; supplier reviews each year.

items.name: Example: a small IT team covers security next to other work

values.details: Two people run IT and security; holidays leave gaps.
values.response: Objective on patching; a stand-in agreed for incidents.

values.needs: Their data kept confidential and available, a signed data processing agreement, and to be told quickly about incidents that affect them.
values.response: Contract terms, incident process, ISO/IEC 27001 certificate.

values.details: Write which sites, teams, services and systems the ISMS covers, what it leaves out and why, and where it meets what others run for you.

sheets.name: Risk treatment plan
sheets.description: How each information security risk is treated: the controls it puts in place, the actions (as sub-items) with owners and due dates, and the residual risk the risk owner accepts. When every action is done the plan goes to the risk owner, then top management, for risk acceptance.

fields.name: Risk owner
fields.description: Approves the plan and accepts the risk that remains once it is done.

fields.name: Annex A controls
fields.description: The Annex A controls this plan puts in place. They show on the requirement and in the statement of applicability.

fields.name: Acceptance step
fields.description: Where the plan is in its risk acceptance. Set by the Risk acceptance workflow, never by hand.

items.name: Example: multi-factor sign-in on every account

values.details: Turn on multi-factor sign-in for email, the office suite and the admin consoles; block legacy sign-in.
Turn on full-disk encryption through device management and report the laptops that are not encrypted.

values.likelihood_scale: 1 Rare: never seen here or at similar organisations. 2 Unlikely: seen at similar organisations. 3 Possible: happened here before. 4 Likely: happens most years. 5 Almost certain: happens several times a year.
values.impact_scale: 1 Negligible: no data exposed, no downtime that customers notice. 2 Minor: a few records or a short outage, handled in a day. 3 Moderate: customers affected or a report to an authority. 4 Major: many customers affected, a contract or certificate at risk. 5 Severe: lasting harm to people whose data it is, or the business stops.

fields.name: Asset or process
fields.description: What the risk is to: the information, system, service or process.

fields.name: Annex A controls
fields.description: The Annex A controls from the ISO/IEC 27001 library that treat this risk.

fields.name: Residual score
fields.description: Likelihood times impact once the treatment plan is done.

config.expr: IF({iso27001_residual_score} = 0, "", IF(EMPTY({appetite}), "No appetite set", IF({iso27001_residual_score} > {appetite}, "Above appetite", "Within appetite")))

values.cause: Not every account has multi-factor sign-in
values.consequence: Customer data read or mail sent in our name

items.name: Example: lost or stolen laptop exposes customer data

values.cause: Laptops travel; some disks are not encrypted

layout.title: Record an information security risk
layout.description: Three short steps: what is at risk and how, how likely and how bad it would be, then who owns it. Choose it in Sheet settings › New item form to ask it when someone adds a risk.

fields.label: What is at risk?
fields.help: The information, system, service or process.

fields.label: What weakness would let it happen?

fields.name: Annex A controls
fields.description: The Annex A controls this control meets. They show on the requirement and in the statement of applicability.

items.name: Example: multi-factor sign-in for every account
Example: security awareness training every year
Example: daily backups, restore tested each quarter
Example: security review of a supplier before signing

automations.name: Control failing → put its risks back into treatment and tell the risk owners
automations.description: A control that fails no longer protects the risks it treats. Every risk linked to it goes back to Being treated, so the risk register shows the gap, and the control owner is told to fix it or plan a replacement.

actions.message: {id} {name} is failing. The risks it treats are back in treatment: fix it or plan a replacement.

automations.name: Control test 14 days late → tell the owner and top management
automations.description: Escalation: the owner is reminded by the Core automation before the test date. When a control of the ISMS is still not tested 14 days after its date, top management hears about it with the owner, because untested controls are an audit finding.

actions.message: {id} {name} was due for testing on {next_test} and has not been tested.

fields.name: Confidentiality need
fields.description: 1 low, 2 medium, 3 high: how much harm disclosure would do.

fields.name: Requirement it meets
fields.description: The ISO/IEC 27001 clause or control this document is evidence for.

automations.name: ISMS document review 14 days late → tell the owner and top management
automations.description: Escalation: Core reminds the owner 30 days before the review date. An ISMS document still not reviewed 14 days after it goes to top management with the owner, since an out-of-date controlled document is an audit finding.

actions.message: {id} {name} was due for review on {next_review}. Review it, or mark it obsolete.

values.kpi: Share of staff who completed the training

values.kpi: Share of critical updates installed within 14 days

automations.name: ISMS management review held → plan the next one in 12 months
automations.description: Recurring review cycle: when an ISMS management review is marked held, the next one is added for a year later, so the yearly review is never forgotten.

fields.name: Containment clock
fields.description: 24 hours from noticing a security incident to containing it.

layout.title: Report a security incident
layout.description: Tell us as soon as you notice something that could put information at risk: a phishing email you clicked, a lost or stolen device, data sent to the wrong person, a system behaving strangely. You do not need to be sure it is an incident.

fields.label: What happened
fields.help: What you saw, when and where, and anything you have already done about it.

fields.label: Which systems or data are affected?
fields.help: For example a laptop, an email account or a customer list. Write "Not sure" if you do not know.

fields.label: How serious do you think it is?
fields.help: Your best guess. The incident handler decides.

fields.label: Your name
fields.help: So the incident handler can reach you.

settings.confirmation: Thank you. The incident handler has your report and will contact you if they need more.

notice.purpose: To handle information security incidents and learn from them.
notice.recipients: The people in this workspace who handle security incidents.
notice.retention: Kept for 3 years after the incident is closed.
notice.rights: You can ask to see, correct or delete what you reported. Contact the person who shared this form.

items.name: Example: phishing email clicked, password changed the same day

values.iso27001_description: A staff member entered their password on a fake sign-in page. IT reset the password and checked the sign-in log within two hours.
values.iso27001_affected: One email account; no sign-in from outside found
values.root_cause: The account did not have multi-factor sign-in yet.

automations.name: Security incident reported → tell the investigator

actions.message: New security incident {id} {name}. Contain it within 24 hours of {iso27001_detected}.

automations.name: Security incident: 12 hours left to contain it → tell the investigator
automations.description: SLA clock, first rung: a security incident should be contained within 24 hours of being noticed. With 12 hours left and no containment time recorded, the investigator and the information security officer are reminded.

actions.message: {id} {name}: 12 hours left to contain it. Record the time it was contained.

automations.name: Serious security incident about to miss its 24 hours → tell top management
automations.description: SLA clock, last rung of the escalation ladder: a medium or high security incident still not contained in the last hour of its 24-hour clock goes to top management, with the investigator, so they can add people or decide what to tell customers.

actions.message: {id} {name} has less than an hour left of its 24 hours to be contained. Decide on more help and on telling customers.

automations.name: Security incident closed and needs a root cause → raise a nonconformity
automations.description: Cross-sheet cascade: closing a security incident marked Needs a root cause raises a linked item in Nonconformities and CAPA, where the root cause, the corrective actions and the effectiveness check are tracked until the nonconformity can close.

layout.title: Report a problem
layout.description: Something that does not meet a requirement of the ISMS: a control not working, a procedure not followed, an audit or review finding.
layout.nameLabel: What is wrong, in one line

settings.confirmation: Thank you. The ISMS owner will look at it and may ask you for more.

items.name: Example: leaver accounts still active after 30 days

values.iso27001_details: Two of ten sampled leavers still had active accounts a month after leaving.
values.iso27001_correction: Both accounts disabled the day they were found.

automations.name: ISMS nonconformity 14 days overdue → tell top management
automations.description: Escalation ladder: Core tells the owner the day a nonconformity is overdue. If an ISMS nonconformity is still open 14 days after its due date, top management is told with the owner, so a stuck corrective action gets resources or a new date.

actions.message: {id} {name} was due on {due_date} and is still at {stage}. Agree resources or a new date.

automations.name: Scope or context review in 30 days → ask the owner for an update

actions.message: Check {id} {name} is still right before {next_review}, and move the review date on.

automations.name: Treatment plan overdue → tell the plan owner and the risk owner

actions.message: {id} {name} was due on {due_date} and is not done.

automations.name: Treatment action overdue → tell the action owner

actions.message: The action "{name}" ({sheet}) was due on {due_date} and is not done.

automations.name: Every treatment action done → submit the plan for risk acceptance
automations.description: Gate: a treatment plan is not finished until its risk owner, then top management, accept the risk that remains. When the last action is done the plan is submitted to the Risk acceptance workflow; it can only reach Residual risk accepted through that approval.

setup.title: ISO 27001 setup
setup.description: Four steps from the Core registers to an ISMS you can audit. Each step’s progress comes from your sheets.

steps.title: Define the scope
steps.body: Write down what affects your information security from inside and outside, who expects what from you, and which parts of the organisation the ISMS covers. Have top management approve the scope statement.

steps.title: Decide which controls apply
steps.body: Mark every Annex A control applicable or not, with a reason, in the statement of applicability. Link the controls you rely on from the Controls library.

steps.title: Plan your risk treatment
steps.body: For each information security risk above appetite, add a treatment plan with an owner, a due date, the Annex A controls it puts in place and the risk owner who will accept what remains.

steps.title: Get the residual risk accepted
steps.body: When a plan’s actions are done it goes to the risk owner, then top management. Give someone the job title Top management so the approval has someone to ask.

apps.title: ISMS CAPA
apps.description: Report nonconformities, work on your corrective actions and check that they worked.

screens.title: Report a problem
screens.description: Say what does not meet a requirement. It goes to Open nonconformities.

screens.title: My actions
screens.description: Actions assigned to you that are not done, soonest first.
screens.empty: No open actions are assigned to you.

screens.title: Needs my check
screens.description: Nonconformities you own whose actions are done and wait for your effectiveness check.
screens.empty: Nothing waits for your effectiveness check.
